bull.b: Sustained top-line growth and recent strong Q1 YoY acceleration indicate product-market fit and expanding commercial traction. Over 2–6 months this growth improves operating leverage potential, expands addressable market reach, and increases the company’s capacity to invest in R&D and sales to support further scale.

Material multi‑customer engagements create backbone revenue opportunities and pipeline visibility beyond spot sales. If contracts convert, they provide multi‑quarter revenue backstop, improve production planning, and strengthen credibility with partners and channel customers, supporting durable commercial expansion.

bull.t: AI Services Strategy and Margin Upside
bull.b: Shifting toward recurring, application‑level AI services diversifies revenue away from one‑time hardware sales and targets higher per‑query margins. Over the medium term this can materially bolster gross margin sustainability and predictable recurring cash flows as services scale and complement hybrid hardware offerings.

bear.t: High Cash Burn and Negative Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Persistent, large negative operating and free cash flows create ongoing funding dependency and limit strategic flexibility. Even with a recent raise, continued cash burn increases dilution risk, constrains capital allocation to growth initiatives, and leaves execution contingent on further financing or rapid margin improvement.

A single large customer accounting for over half of guidance concentrates revenue risk: delivery timing, conversion, or contract changes can materially swing reported results. This dependence reduces revenue visibility, weakens bargaining leverage, and elevates downside if the relationship delays or scales slower than expected.

bear.t: Supply-Chain HBM Shortage and Near-Term Margin Pressure
bear.b: External HBM constraints force reliance on third‑party hardware and delay Blaize‑powered server deployments, compressing blended margins and slowing margin recovery. Supply fragility can push meaningful margin and revenue improvement further into the back half of the year, prolonging cash burn and execution risk.
